description: Tall, thin-stemmed verbena holding flat heads of small purple flowers well above its foliage. Named for Buenos Aires, and one of the hardest working nectar plants you can put in a garden.
nativeStatus: Native to the Río de la Plata region
ecology: A grassland and open-ground perennial. Flowers for months, then sets a heavy seed crop, so it feeds insects and then birds from the same plant.
wildlifeNotes: Butterflies work it constantly through the warm season and hummingbirds visit it. Once the heads go over, small seed-eating birds strip the seed. Leave the spent stems standing for them.
size: Tall and narrow, to about 1.5 m
flowering: Long warm season, well into autumn
propagation: Self-sows freely. Move seedlings while they are small, or leave them to fill gaps.
